t: Mutsuhito came to the throne as a boy in 1867, and in his name the Satsuma and Chōshū samurai overthrew the Tokugawa shogunate and proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule in 1868.

His reign saw the domains abolished, the samurai's privileges ended, a cabinet, constitution and Diet created, and victories over China and Russia, with the annexation of Taiwan in 1895 and Korea in 1910.
How much power he held himself is disputed: he kept no diary and wrote almost no letters, and historians call him anything from a figurehead to an autocrat.
dyk: Meiji's waka asking why wind and waves rise in discord when the seas of the four directions are all born of one womb was recited by his grandson Emperor Shōwa at an Imperial Conference in September 1941, before the attack on Pearl Harbor.
ev: Prince Mutsuhito is born in Kyoto
On the death of Emperor Kōmei he becomes emperor at fourteen
The restoration of imperial rule is proclaimed, the Charter Oath is issued and Edo is renamed Tokyo
The domains are abolished and Japan is organised into prefectures
Japan annexes Taiwan after its victory in the First Sino-Japanese War
Korea is annexed by the Empire of Japan
The emperor dies in Tokyo and is succeeded by Yoshihito

f.born: 3 November 1852 in a house on his maternal grandfather's property at the north end of the Gosho, Kyoto; son of Emperor Kōmei and his concubine Nakayama Yoshiko
f.died: 29 July 1912 at Meiji Palace, Tokyo, aged 59, of uremia, suffering from diabetes, nephritis and gastroenteritis
f.role: Crown prince from 1860; Emperor of Japan from 1867 until his death in 1912
f.known: the Meiji Restoration; the Charter Oath (1868); moving the capital to Tokyo; the Meiji Constitution (1889); the Imperial Rescript on Education (1890); the Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese wars
